concepts.title: Hamming distance and the Singleton bound
concepts.blurb: A block code $C\subseteq\Sigma^n$ has parameters $[n,k,d]_q$ where $|C|=q^k$ and $d=\min_{c\neq c'}d_H(c,c')$. The code corrects $t=\lfloor (d-1)/2\rfloor$ errors because closed Hamming balls of radius $t$ around distinct codewords are disjoint. Singleton's elementary puncturing argument forces $d\le n-k+1$; codes meeting this with equality are MDS.

concepts.title: Linear codes: generator, parity-check, syndrome
concepts.blurb: A linear $[n,k]$ code is a $k$-dimensional subspace of $\mathbb{F}_q^n$, described either by a generator matrix $G$ (rows span $C$) or a parity-check $H$ (kernel is $C$). The minimum distance equals the smallest number of linearly dependent columns of $H$. Given $y=c+e$, the syndrome $Hy^\top=He^\top$ depends only on the error pattern; syndrome decoding looks up the minimum-weight coset leader.

concepts.title: Hamming codes
concepts.blurb: For each $m\ge 2$ the binary Hamming code $\mathrm{Ham}(m)$ has parameters $[2^m-1,2^m-1-m,3]$. Its parity-check matrix has every non-zero column of $\mathbb{F}_2^m$. The code is perfect: balls of radius $1$ tile $\mathbb{F}_2^n$. Arranging columns as binary representations of $1,\dots,n$ makes the syndrome literally point at the flipped bit.

concepts.title: Reed–Solomon codes
concepts.blurb: Encode messages as polynomials $f\in\mathbb{F}_q[x]_{<k}$ and transmit their values $f(\alpha_1),\dots,f(\alpha_n)$ at $n\le q$ distinct points. Two degree-$<k$ polynomials agree at $\le k-1$ points, so $d=n-k+1$ exactly — Reed–Solomon codes are MDS. Berlekamp–Massey, Berlekamp–Welch, and Guruswami–Sudan decoders all exploit this algebraic structure.

concepts.title: BCH codes
concepts.blurb: A cyclic code is an ideal in $\mathbb{F}_q[x]/(x^n-1)$, generated by a divisor $g(x)$ of $x^n-1$. The BCH construction picks $g$ as the $\mathrm{lcm}$ of minimal polynomials of $\delta-1$ consecutive powers of a primitive $n$-th root of unity. The BCH bound guarantees $d\ge\delta$ via a Vandermonde determinant; cyclotomic cosets dictate which extra roots come along for free.

concepts.title: LDPC codes and belief propagation
concepts.blurb: Gallager's low-density parity-check codes use a sparse random $H$ with constant row and column weights, described by a bipartite Tanner graph. Belief-propagation decoding passes log-likelihood-ratio messages between variable and check nodes; for well-designed irregular ensembles this approaches the Shannon limit within $\sim 0.0045\,\mathrm{dB}$. The mathematics is density evolution on the message distribution.

concepts.title: Lattice codes and sphere packings
concepts.blurb: A lattice $\Lambda\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ packs spheres of radius $\lambda_1/2$ with center density $(\lambda_1/2)^n/\det\Lambda$. Construction A lifts a binary linear code to a lattice; the extended Hamming $[8,4,4]$ gives $E_8$ and the binary Golay $[24,12,8]$ gives the Leech lattice. Viazovska's 2016 proof that $E_8$ and (with collaborators) the Leech lattice are optimal closed two long-standing problems.
